finding.claim: The pub router's POST /hooks/test sends an axios POST to a URL taken straight from the request body. Nothing in the file validates the scheme, host, or resolved IP, and no authentication middleware is applied to the pub router in this file. Any caller who can reach the route can make the server request internal hosts or cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The response status is returned to the caller, which gives a port and host oracle. axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker-hosted redirect also works.

trace.note: pub = express.Router(); requireAdmin is not applied to it
req.body.callback is passed unmodified to axios.post
r.status is returned to the caller, so the response is partly visible

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, DNS resolution or private-IP check, and no redirect restriction (axios maxRedirects is left at its default). The only auth middleware in the file is requireAdmin, which is attached to the admin router only (line 12). Auth for pub could be applied where the router is mounted, but that code is not in this directory.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback unvalidated to axios.post, and the pub router (routes.js:4, handler at 19) has no auth or validation, since requireAdmin is only applied to admin at routes.js:12; the status is returned at routes.js:21. Mount-level auth is outside this directory, but nothing here prevents the SSRF.

finding.claim: The admin router's GET /diagnostics/fetch fetches a URL taken from the query string with axios.get. It has no scheme, host or IP validation. An admin session is required, so the attacker must be an admin or must have taken over an admin session. An admin of a multi-tenant deployment can still reach internal services or cloud metadata, and the response status is returned. This is a lower-severity finding than ssrf-1, but there is no destination restriction.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates every route on the admin router
req.query.url is passed unmodified to axios.get
r.status is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin enforces the admin role, which limits who can reach the sink. There is no URL scheme or host allowlist, no private-IP or metadata blocking, and no redirect limit.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) restricts the route to session role "admin". This is an authorization gate, not a URL validation guard. No URL scheme or host validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace matches routes.js:7-16, but the sink at routes.js:15 is only reachable through admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which requires req.session.role === "admin". Only an admin can control req.query.url, so it is not attacker-controlled by an unauthenticated or low-privilege user.
